### A history step left the sheet over another venue (2026-09-17, sw.js v174)

The movie sheet is modal: opening it marks the header and the list behind it inert.
`hashchange` was the only thing that closed it from the URL, and a traversal that changes
`?area=` and `#m=` in one step fires `popstate` alone. So Back across a venue left the
previous cinema's film, with that cinema's ticket links, over a page nothing could touch;
the only exits were Escape, the overlay or the drag gesture. Back to the chooser was worse:
`showHome` clears `state.area`, and `syncSheet` returns early without one, so no later
hashchange could close it either.

`onPopState` now handles the sheet in each branch. Leaving a venue closes it before the
new schedule is asked for, then reopens it from the entry's fragment once that venue's
shows are in; the film resolves against that venue's data, and the sheet says so when it
has none. The step to the chooser closes it. A hash-only step is left alone, because
`hashchange` fires for it and owns the fragment; doing it here too would redraw the sheet
twice for one step, which a test already pinned as changing nothing.

Three branches were written and then removed for being unobservable: closing the sheet
where nothing is selected at all, making `syncSheet` close it with no area, and acting only
on a disagreement between the fragment and the open sheet. Only venue picks push history
entries, every other URL change being a `replaceState`, so a same-area traversal always
carries a fragment change and the chooser branch already closes the sheet.

The fixture gained a second venue, Promenadi Pori, showing a film no other venue in it
does, so a sheet left over from one cinema is identifiable in the other's page by its
title. The mid-load window took more. A traversal refetches nothing, since the venue
returned to is already in `jsonCache`; a reload empties the cache and keeps the history,
and the file then came from the browser's HTTP cache, so the fixture answers a delayed file
`no-store` as well. That leaves a second of flight to observe, and the ordering mutation
goes red.

Tests: six in `tests/browser`, four in `tests/test_home_flow.py` through the harness that
drives `onPopState` without a DOM, where the order against the load is what is asserted.
Five mutations, all red.

Added 2026-09-17, after review found it uncovered: the `state.area === id` guard on the
reopen. It carries the claim above, that the sheet comes back only once that venue's shows
are in, and dropping it left every test green. It is exercised by a venue file released
after the reader has gone back to the chooser, where the entry's `#m=` would otherwise open
that venue's film over the chooser. The opposite scenario, the same load arriving while the
reader is still on the venue that named it, is asserted beside it, so the guard cannot be
satisfied by never reopening. Three mutations, all red: guard dropped, reopen removed,
comparison inverted.

### hideSheet cleared an inert flag it had not set (2026-09-17, sw.js v175)

Three modals drive one boolean. The month picker, the venue picker and the movie sheet
each call `BEHIND().forEach(el => setInert(el, ...))` on the header, the list and the
footer, so whichever closes last decides what the page behind them is. `hideSheet` cleared
it outside its own `wasOpen` guard, which until 2026-09-17 cost nothing: every caller
closed a sheet that was open.

`25a7cc38` added two callers that do not. `onPopState` calls `hideSheet` on every traversal
that leaves a venue or reaches the chooser, whether a sheet is open or not, so a Back
pressed with the venue picker open handed the page back from under it: `#vwrap` still
`open`, `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`, and `main`, `header` and `footer` all tabbable
and exposed to a screen reader again, with the picker's own document-level `vKey` still
taking Escape and the arrows for whatever was focused behind it. The month picker is the
same shape. Nothing re-inerted until the picker was closed and reopened.

The correction is the guard the focus restore already had, `if(wasOpen)`. A modal then
clears only what it set, and that is what lets three of them share one flag. Gating the two
new calls in `onPopState` would have left the next unconditional caller to find this again.

Found by review of `25a7cc38`, and measured in a browser before it was believed: at that
commit the picker stays open with nothing inert behind it, and at its parent all three stay
inert. The month picker was checked the same way on 2026-09-17, across Back and Forward:
open, header, main and footer inert, focus inside the picker; with the unconditional clear
restored the three flags read false from the Back step onward.

Tests: three in `tests/browser/test_client_browser.py`, covering Back with the picker open,
the ordinary close afterwards, and a traversal with no modal open. Two mutations: the
unconditional clear restored reds the first; the clear removed altogether reds five, so the
guard cannot be satisfied by never clearing.

### The landing pages on a phone: a full-width list and quieter cinema links (2026-09-18)

Both halves of "Landing pages: two open items", recorded 2026-09-02 and built together
because they touch the same file and the same pages. `scripts/build_pages.py` alone; the
app is not involved and neither is `DESIGN.md`, whose ticket values this change reads and
does not move.

**The list was trapped in the information column.** `.film` is a flex row of poster and
`.info`, and the `<ul class="times">` sits inside `.info`, so on a phone every ticket was
laid out in the narrow column beside the poster while the space under the poster stayed
empty. The markup is unchanged. Inside the existing 560 px breakpoint the poster floats left and
the list clears it: the header text wraps beside the poster and the list goes underneath at
the full width, whether the header is taller than the poster or shorter. Measured on the Helsinki city page: at 393 px the list went
from the 275 px column to the film's full 365 px, at 320 px to 292 of 292, at 560 px to 532
of 532. A four-screening film that stacked three tickets and clipped the fourth now lays
them out two by two.

**Desktop keeps the flex row and is untouched, which is why the breakpoint owns all of
it.** The first attempt made `.film` a grid at every width, with the list moved out of
`.info` and the poster spanning both rows. That is wrong on desktop for a film whose
`.info` is shorter than the poster: a row-spanning item distributes its height across the
rows it spans, so the 132 px poster inflated row one and pushed the tickets down 28 px.
It hit 10 of the 83 films on the Helsinki page, each of them a title with no metadata and
no synopsis, and the article heights stayed the same, which is what hid it. `min-content`
on the first row does not help, because the spanning item still distributes.

**What desktop identity was measured on.** A signature of every one of the 83 film
articles at 1200 px, ten numbers each: the poster's x, y and width, the title's x and y,
the list's x, y, width and height, and the article's height. Before and after hash to the
same value. The page's only change in height is the cinema-links block, 181 px to 165 px,
which is the second item below.

**The cinema links were reading as a colour key.** They were bordered chips with a
background, a shadow and a 3 px chain bar, which is the vocabulary the one CTA on the page
should own. They are underlined text links now, in the page's ink, with the chain colour
kept as a 3 px marker at the left edge. This one is deliberately not inside the breakpoint:
the maintainer asked for the same link on the phone and on desktop so the pages read as one
design, and accepted the 16 px the desktop block loses by it. Every one measures 44 px of hit area, `tap.floor`
in `DESIGN.md`, and keyboard focus draws a 2 px accent outline at a 3 px offset;
`:focus-visible` was verified by tabbing to a link, not by calling `focus()`, which does
not set it. Eight distinct chain colours still resolve. "Avaa koko ohjelmisto" is
unchanged and is still the only button.

**What was checked at each width**, 320, 375, 393, 560 and 1200, in both themes and in both
languages: no horizontal overflow at any of them, the longest label
("Gilda Bio Rex Lasipalatsi") fits at 320, per-screening languages still print on their own
stub, priced stubs keep their own amount (18 €, 22 €, 14 € on one page) and the 265 unpriced
ones keep the 16 px tail with both 8 px notches and the dashed seam. A film with no poster
keeps its 72 px blank tile and its title beside it, and its ticket spans the full width
below; a film with no synopsis behaves the same. The ticket itself measures 40 px tall with
a 7 px radius throughout, which is what `DESIGN.md` states.

232 of 237 pages were rewritten. The build is deterministic: a second and third
`--date recorded` run wrote nothing. Tests: the full suite 2129, with
`tests/test_landing_pages.py` 122 and `tests/test_design_contract.py` 9 green unchanged.


### The phone layout shipped broken on WebKit, and the fix is a float (2026-09-18, later)

The change above first shipped as a grid. Inside the breakpoint `.film` became a
two-column grid, `.info` became `display:contents` so the header parts were the grid's own
items, and the poster took `grid-row:1/-2` to span every row but the list's, because the
number of header rows depends on what a film has.

**`1/-2` means nothing here.** A negative grid line resolves against the *explicit* grid,
and the rule declared `grid-template-columns` only, so there were no explicit rows to
count back from. Chromium laid it out as intended. WebKit did not: it put the poster in
row one, the row grew to the poster's height, and the metadata and the synopsis started
below the poster with the title stranded at the top. That is what an iPhone showed on
leffavuoro.fi, and it was reproduced on the iOS simulator against the live site before
anything was changed.

**Every check that passed it.** The suite reads markup. The design contract reads numbers
out of the CSS. The browser check written the same day drove Chromium only, and its own
phone assertion read the heading's *box*, which stays beside the poster in both engines.
Three layers, none of which could see it.

**The fix is a float**, which needs no row arithmetic: the poster floats left, the header
text wraps beside it, and `clear` puts the list underneath at the full width. It behaves
the same whether the header is taller or shorter than the poster, and it is the same in
both engines.

Verified in WebKit as well as Chromium, and on the iOS simulator. The browser check now
takes `KINO_BROWSER_ENGINE`, asserts text rectangles measured with a Range rather than
boxes, and pins the part *after* the title as the thing that has to begin while the poster
is still beside it. Against the source that shipped, that test fails in WebKit and passes
in Chromium, which is the shape of the fault.
### What survives a service-worker version bump (2026-09-19)

`activate` dropped every cache whose key was not the current one, for the reason its
comment gave: an old `index.html` must not come back as the offline fallback. What the
comment did not account for is that the new cache is **empty** at that moment. A worker
activates after a navigation the *old* worker served, and the page is network-first, so
nothing had written the new version's cache. Deleting the old one there threw away the
schedule JSON and every mirrored poster as well as the shell, and a reader who closed the
tab got nothing at all on the next offline launch.

- **`/data/` migrates, the shell does not.** The schedule and the posters are the entries
  the new version has no copy of and no reason to refuse; `index.html` is the one the
  delete was written for. Carrying it over would have reversed that decision, which a
  first attempt did before review caught it, and it is not reversed here.
- **Only this app's caches are deleted.** The sweep took every unrecognised key, which on
  a shared origin is another tool's storage. `OWNED = /^leffavuoro-v(\d+)$/` now bounds it.
- **The newest old cache is read first** and an entry the new version already holds is
  never overwritten, so a two-version jump cannot resurrect the older of the two.

Covered by `tests/sw_activate_harness.js` and `ServiceWorkerActivationTest`: a stub Cache
Storage, activate driven for real, and the entries tagged with the cache they came from so
"kept what this version already has" is an assertion about which copy survived. Three
mutations go red, including migrating the shell.

**Left open:** the shell is still absent offline for one load after an update. Precaching
it on install is the fix that needs neither the old copy nor a network, and that is the
maintainer's call; the `IDEAS.md` entry carries it.

### A film's original release year on the card (2026-09-20, sw.js v194)
"Carrie (1976)" on the card and on its sheet. A year is what tells a reader the 19:00
showing is a revival rather than this week's release, and the same suffix on everything
now playing would be noise on almost every card, so it appears only for a film at least
two calendar years old: `oyear < currentYear - 1`, which in 2026 shows 2024 and older and
leaves 2025 and 2026 bare. The boundary is a whole calendar year rather than a rolling
date so it does not move under a reader in December, and `currentYear` is Europe/Helsinki's
so it does not change for a reader abroad.

**The year is the film's own, and three nearby years are not it.** This is the whole
difficulty, and none of it is visible in a screenshot:

- Finnkino's `releaseDate`, which `fetch_data.py` already reads, is the *Finnish* release.
  For a reissue that is this year, so it would print "Carrie (2026)" on the one kind of
  film the feature exists for.
- `show["year"]` is whatever the cinema printed. Two adapters set it, `gather()` collects
  it as a hint for the TMDB search, and nothing checks it against anything.
- The screening's own date is never the film's.

So `oyear` is written from an exact TMDB match's `release_date` and from nothing else. It
is captured off the `/movie/{id}` response the pass already fetches, so it costs no
request, and it is published behind `trusted()`, the same gate as `tmdbId`, because a weak
candidate's year belongs to a different film. It is in `PUBLISHED`, so it comes back off a
row whose entry stops being trusted. A missing year stays missing: no fallback, no
inference, and no year read out of a title.

**Two implementations, one table.** `filmTitle()` in index.html renders the card and the
sheet; `build_pages.film_title` renders the static pages. A reader following a link from
one to the other must not see the film renamed, so both are driven from the same `CASES`
list in tests/test_release_year.py and a change to either that the other does not follow
fails there. The clock is a parameter in both and never `today()`, which is what makes the
boundary cases assertable.

**What real data caught that the specification did not.** Seven published titles already
end in a year -- "Trainspotting (1996)", "Twin Peaks: Kausi 1 (1990)" -- and appending
would have rendered "Trainspotting (1996) (1996)". A title that already carries a year
keeps it and gets no second one, whether or not it agrees with TMDB's: the cinema has
already answered the question the suffix exists to answer. Found by running the pass and
reading the rows, not by the case list.

**No image carries a year.** The blank tile's two letters come off the bare `title`, not
off the formatted string, or "Carrie (1976)" would tile as "C1"; verified live as "RJ" on
a poster-less row. Posters and the Heureka title cards carry none either: an image cannot
be relocalised or corrected and would go stale in the file.

`sheetCtx.title` stays bare, so the share text and the .ics file are unchanged. The
JSON-LD `name` stays bare too, and so does the `films-extra.json` key, which is the same
title `normTitle()` groups on: nothing about matching or grouping moved.

Coverage fills over time rather than at once. `ry` is written when an entry is searched or
re-read, and the refresh budget is twelve a run, so the 537 cached titles fill over some
days. That is correct rather than a gap: a title with no `ry` shows no year.

Tests: 13 in tests/test_release_year.py over 21 cases, including the four years around the
boundary, seven malformed values, the reissue, the already-dated titles, and the three
year sources that must not be read. 14 mutations, every one red, across the client, the
page generator and the publish gate.

### A pending venue says it has no programme (2026-09-20, sw.js v195)
`run.py` separates three empty venues: `pending`, where the adapter confirmed the upstream
answered and listed nothing; `stale`, which keeps its previous programme; and `unverified`,
which has never had data and must stay visibly degraded. Only `/status/` read that. The app
said "Ei enää näytöksiä tänään" about a cinema closed for the season, on every date the
reader tried, and `L.noProgYet` had sat defined and unused in all three languages since
`healthState` moved to the status page.

**No new request.** The flag comes off the `venues-{provider}.json` already being parsed
for its venue list, marked per venue while that list is built.

**The decision is `pendingNotice(ids, pendingIds, hasShows)`, pure and narrow.** It never
fires while the payload carries a screening anywhere, which is what keeps filter-empty,
past-horizon and ordinary empty days on their own messages; `unverified` is empty too but
is not in `pending`, so it keeps its degraded state, which is the distinction `run.py`
exists to make; and a combined city or region needs **every** member pending, because one
quiet cinema beside one that is playing is not a city with nothing on. It is decided ahead
of the filter and date branches in `emptyMsg()`, so a confirmed-empty cinema is never
described as a filter result. `emptyStatus()` calls `emptyMsg()`, so the status line
follows without a second change.

Verified live against Tähti Kino, which was genuinely pending in the committed data:
"Ei ohjelmistoa juuri nyt", "Inget program just nu", "No programme right now". Espoo, four
venues and none pending, still drew 22 cards, and a search matching nothing there still
said so rather than claiming the city had no programme. Muhos is in no region and no
multi-venue city, so the combined cases have no live instance and are covered by the table
in tests/test_pending_state.py.

Tests: 10, over 14 cases plus the wiring read out of `index.html`. 6 mutations, every one
red, including reversing the precedence against the filter branch.

### PostHog analytics, cookieless (2026-09-20, sw.js v196)
Added on the maintainer's explicit instruction, superseding the "no third-party requests"
property held since 2026-08-29. Public project token, PostHog EU Cloud. One service, two
requests: the bundle from eu-assets.i.posthog.com and the events to eu.i.posthog.com.
The bundle is pinned to 1.434.2, the version the payload below was measured against; the
version path segment is honoured (1.400.0 serves a different bundle, unknown versions
404). Analytics covers the interactive app only, not the generated pages or /status/.

Cookieless, not anonymous: PostHog receives the network IP and hashes it server-side into
a privacy-preserving identifier. No cookies, browser-storage identifiers, person profiles,
advertising, cross-site tracking or session recordings. It is not claimed that no personal
data is processed.

Seven events: page_view (category), area_opened (kind, area), cinema_opened (venue),
date_changed (offset_days), language_changed (lang), search_used (nothing), ticket_opened
(provider). `analyticsScrub` is posthog-js `before_send` and enforces both the event list
and the per-event property list.

Measured on the wire, posthog-js 1.434.2, with a title and query planted in the call:

    {"api_key":"phc_...","batch":[{"uuid":"...","event":"cinema_opened",
      "properties":{"venue":"tahtikino-muhos","token":"phc_...",
                    "distinct_id":"$posthog_cookieless"},
      "timestamp":"..."}],"sent_at":"..."}

The library attaches 43 properties before before_send, including $current_url, $pathname,
$host, $referrer, $raw_user_agent, $browser*, $os*, $device_type, $screen_* and
$timezone*. All stripped. `forbidden_event` was dropped.

**Mandatory, cannot be removed:** `token` and `distinct_id` in properties; strip either
and posthog-js builds no request at all, silently. Bisected 2026-09-20. `distinct_id` is
the constant `$posthog_cookieless`. Envelope carries api_key, uuid, timestamp, sent_at.

Three findings that cost time:
- The bundle is at `eu-assets.i.posthog.com/static/array.js`, not the API host.
- `has_opted_out_capturing()` returns true whenever `cookieless_mode:'always'` is set. It
  does not block capture. Red herring.
- `advanced_disable_decide:true` is kept: no config.js request, and events still send.

Notice at /tietosuoja/, fi/sv/en, retention one year (Free plan, confirmed by the
maintainer). Project settings confirmed in the fetched config.js: autocapture, heatmaps,
session recording, surveys, web vitals, console logs and exception capture all off.

Not instrumented: the generated landing pages and /status/. Analytics is the app only.

### Analytics corrections: $pageview, pinned bundle, production-host guard (2026-09-20, v197)
Four narrow changes on the maintainer's instruction, all measured.

**$pageview replaces the custom page_view**, so PostHog Web Analytics counts it. It
carries `category` and a synthetic `$current_url` of `https://leffavuoro.fi/app/{category}`
(home, venue, city, region), built from the category alone. The browser's real URL, path
and query never reach it, and every other URL, referrer and device property stays
stripped. It is the only event allowed to carry a URL at all.

**Bundle pinned to 1.434.2**, `/static/1.434.2/array.js`. The version segment is real:
1.400.0 serves a different 227 kB bundle, 1.200.0 and 9.9.9 return 404. Without the pin a
PostHog default change would move the contract this file documents.

**Production-host guard.** `phAllowedOrigin(protocol, hostname)` allows exactly
`https:` + `leffavuoro.fi`. Checked before the script element is created, and again in
`track()` and `trackTicket()` before anything is queued, so a rejected origin makes no
request and fills no queue a later init could flush. Exact hostname match, no suffix test:
`leffavuoro.fi.evil.example` and `www.leffavuoro.fi` are both refused, as are localhost,
127.0.0.1, [::1], file:, github.io and unrelated domains. Verified on 127.0.0.1: `posthog`
undefined, no script element, zero requests, including after a ticket click. DNT and GPC
checks are unchanged and still run first.

**Wording.** One third-party *service*, not one request: the bundle and the events are
separate requests.

Portability was removed from all three privacy notices. The basis is legitimate interest
under 6(1)(f), and Article 20 covers consent or contract, so the right does not apply;
each notice now says so rather than omitting it silently. Access, rectification, erasure,
restriction and objection are unchanged.

Not done, deliberately: the generated pages and /status/ stay uninstrumented, no extra
PostHog domain was authorized, no internal-user flag or person property was added, and the
~13 localhost events from the wire investigation were left in place.

### A screening's language belongs to the screening (2026-09-20, sw.js v198)
The Helsinki card read "espanja · tekstitys: suomi/ruotsi" for Autofiktio and the film
details, where the booking choices are, said nothing about language at all. Two separate
faults behind one symptom.

**The sheet never drew it.** `showSheet` built `meta1` from `scoreRing`, rating, premiere,
length and formats, and `meta2` from genres. Neither carried `lang`, and nor did the stub.

**The card folded it off the first screening.** `byEvent.set(id, { ...s, times:[] })`
copied the first show's `lang`, and `if(!m.lang && s.lang) m.lang = s.lang;` filled it from
the next one that had any. The comment three lines above already said `lang` "belongs to
the screening"; the fold contradicted it.

**Measured over the committed data that day.** 4,150 shows, 54 distinct `lang` values, 751
of them empty (18.1%). At the scope the client actually renders, 1,469 (area, film) pairs:
73.3% agree on one non-empty value, 24.7% publish none, 1.9% disagree outright and 0.1%
mix a known value with a missing one. Combined city views, 422 pairs, 2.4% mixed with 4
gap-cases. Small, and the case that costs a reader something: Kojootti vs. ACME runs dubbed
(`FI-A`) beside subtitled (`EN-A, FI-S, SV-S`) in one cinema on one day.

**`langSplit(list)` decides it**, pure and sliced by `tests/lang_split_harness.js`.
Agreement puts one line beside the genres in the sheet head and keeps it on the card;
disagreement moves it onto each ticket. One missing value makes the set differing, so a
screening that published nothing stays blank rather than inheriting a neighbour's. This is
the same rule the card already applied to format tags through `common`.

**Nothing new to translate.** `langTxt` already renders audio bare and subtitles labelled
through `LN` and `LW` in all three interface languages, and `applyLang` redraws an open
sheet through `syncSheet`.

**The ticket does not change shape.** `.slang` is the last item in the details
compartment, so it takes a row under the room name inside the existing `.aud`; measured at
390 px the compartment is 34 px inside a 40 px ticket, and every value DESIGN.md pins is
untouched. The card and the sheet legitimately differ: the card folds one day, the sheet
holds every date, so a film can agree on the 14th and disagree across the week.

**Verified in Chromium and WebKit at 390 px and 1200 px, in fi, sv and en**, against
fixtures for all three classes. Shared: one head line, no stub lines. Mixed: no head line,
"suomi" and "englanti · tekstitys: suomi/ruotsi" on their own tickets. Gap: the screening
with no value renders nothing while its neighbour renders its own.

### The stale banner names every late provider and offers one link (2026-09-20, sw.js v199)
Finnkino showed an eight-hour warning during a review. The sentence was accurate and there
was nothing to do with it: no route to the cinema's own programme, and in a combined city
no way to tell which of the cinemas on screen it was about.

**It read one timestamp.** `loadGroup` returned `generated`, the oldest part, and `oldest`,
that part's provider. Two late providers in one city therefore named one of them, which
reads as a claim that the rest are current. The fold now also returns `sources`, each
provider with its own oldest part, and a single venue synthesises the same shape from its
file and its registry provider.

**`staleNotice(sources, nowMs, staleH)` decides it**, pure and sliced by
`tests/stale_notice_harness.js`. Every provider past the threshold is named, oldest first,
and the age reported is the oldest. A part with no timestamp, or one `Date.parse` cannot
read, is never called late: unknown stays unknown. The comparison is strict, so exactly
`STALE_H` old is not late.

**One late provider gets its own site; two get `/status/`.** The host is
`SOURCE[id][1]`, which is the registry's `host` through `data/providers.json`, and the link
is that host's root through `safeUrl`. No programme path is constructed from it: a guessed
path is what left six Nexxo ticket links dead, and the visitor-facing path is each site's
own. With two late providers neither is "the" affected cinema, so the fallback is the
status page carrying the current `area` and `lang`, built by `statusHref()` -- extracted
from `renderContact` so the footer link and the banner cannot drift apart.

**No "reload".** A refresh re-reads this origin's committed files and starts no collection
at any cinema, so neither label says so. `staleSite` names the host, `staleStatus` names
the status page, both in fi, sv and en.

**Styled as the footer's link out**, accent text with no box, and the 44 px of hit area
come from `.pastlink`'s padding-cancelled-by-negative-margin, so the banner keeps the
height it had and no new visual element is introduced.

**Verified in Chromium and WebKit.** Single cinema at 320, 390 and 1200 px in all three
languages: 44 px or more, no horizontal overflow, `https://cinemaorion.fi/`, and the label
follows the language toggle. Combined Helsinki with two providers: both late names both and
links `/status/?area=city%3AHelsinki`; either one late names that one and links its own
host. Swedish at 320 px wraps the label to two lines at 56 px.

### Report incorrect details, from the screening menu (2026-09-20, sw.js v200)
A reader who spots a wrong time has the cinema, the film and the minute on screen and no
way to say so. A third row in the ticket's own menu, after share and calendar.

**The app carries no address.** The three copies in `index.html`, `build_pages.py` and the
client's `CONTACT` constant went on 2026-09-07 so a rotation has one place to reach, and
`tests/test_contact_address.py` fails if either file grows one back. The first attempt
here put the constant back and that test caught it. So the app links: the row navigates to
`/status/?report=<detail>#contact`, and the status page, which owns the one copy in static
markup, composes the draft onto its existing `mailto:` anchor and swaps `contactLead` for a
line saying the draft is ready. With no `report` on the query that page is unchanged.

**What the draft names.** Film, cinema and room, weekday, date and time, and the
screening's own share URL. Nothing else is read off the page: no search text, no filter
state, no referrer, no user agent, and a test asserts those absences. Nothing is sent --
`location.href` hands a prefilled draft to the reader's own client and they send it.

**Verified in Chromium and WebKit at 320, 390 and 1200 px in fi, sv and en**, 18
combinations: three menu rows at 44 px, the row navigating, and the composed subject and
body read back off the status page. Break-verified with four mutations, including one that
leaks `state.filter` into the draft.

### One cue that the ticket menu exists (2026-09-20, sw.js v201)
Sharing a screening and adding it to a calendar have been behind the ticket's dots since
v151, with an `aria-label` and nothing a sighted reader could see. The cheap fix is a
label on every ticket, which on a film with a long run repeats one instruction fifty
times and takes room from the schedule.

**One line per sheet instead**, between the synopsis and the first day, so it sits beside
the tickets it describes rather than on them. Muted, `.78rem`, one line at 390 px and
wrapping to two in Swedish and English at 320 px. It carries the button's own `DOTS`
svg inline rather than naming it, so it points at the control.

**Drawn only where a ticket has a menu.** `all.some(x => x.start >= now)`: a sheet whose
every screening has gone gets no menus and no cue. A sheet with nothing in it gets none
either, since it is gated on `days`.

**Not above the synopsis.** The synopsis was clamped to four lines in v137 to keep the
first day above the fold; putting an instruction over it would spend what that bought.

**Verified in Chromium and WebKit at 320, 390 and 1200 px in fi, sv and en**, 18
combinations: exactly one cue, its glyph 14 px, above the first day heading, no overflow
and no clipping. Break-verified with four mutations.

### "Alkaen": a minimum start time in Ajat (2026-09-20, sw.js v202)
Ajat sorted by time and could not narrow by it, so "what can I still see after six" meant
scrolling past the afternoon. A minimum start time, inclusive, in that view only.

**It is a time-of-day question, not a past/future one.** "Starts at or after 18:00" means
the same thing next Saturday as today, so the control is not gated on the date and the
existing past-screening behaviour is untouched. An earlier note had this backwards.

**`startsAtOrAfter(clock, min)`**, pure and sliced by `tests/time_filter_harness.js`.
`clock` is `fiTime(s.start)`, which formats through `Europe/Helsinki`, so a reader abroad
gets Finland wall time. Both sides are zero-padded 24-hour `HH:MM`, which is why a string
compare is a time compare. Inclusive, because that is what *alkaen* says. No restriction
passes everything; a screening with no readable clock is not admitted while one is on.

**Applied in `renderTimes`, not in `passFilters`.** That function is shared with Leffat,
which must not see this. The restriction narrows what the other filters already matched,
so search, chips and the chain restriction keep working and compose with it.

**`state.minTime`, memory only.** A browsing aid for one visit, not a saved preference;
`kino-prefs` still holds venue, theme and favourite and nothing else. It survives a date
change, a cinema change and a trip through Leffat, and a reload starts from all times.

**The control is one native `<select>`** above the list, offering half-hour marks rather
than a free clock: the question is "after six", not "after 18:07", and one tap beats a
spinner. `timeSlots` builds them. On today the list starts half an hour behind the clock,
rounded down, so a screening that has just begun is still reachable; on another day there
is no "now" to sit behind and it starts at the day's first screening. It never starts
before that screening -- at 06:10 with nothing before 20:00, marks from 05:30 would be
thirty options that all mean "all times" -- and it ends at the last screening's mark. "All
times" is the first option rather than a second button, so the reset costs no width. A
value the clock has moved past stays selectable, or the control would read "all times"
while still filtering. No day's screenings, no bar; the value is kept in state regardless.

**36 px to the eye, 44 px of hit area** -- and the first attempt at that shipped the
control unclickable. `.chip` extends its own hit area with an `::after`, which works
because the chip *is* the interactive element. Copying that onto a wrapper around the
select did the opposite: the pseudo-element covered the control, so `elementFromPoint` at
its centre returned the wrapper and a real click did nothing, in Chromium and WebKit
alike, at 320 and 1200 px. It could not have helped even without that, since a wrapper's
pseudo-element is not part of the select. Reported from the live site as v202.

**Why every check passed anyway.** The rig set the value with Playwright's
`select_option` and with `dispatchEvent('change')`. Neither performs a hit test, so both
drove a control no finger could reach. Fixed by making the select itself the hit area:
the wrapper draws the 36 px box, the select sits on it transparent and 44 px tall with
`margin:-4px 0`, and the focus ring moved to `.tfield:focus-within` since the select's own
outline is suppressed. `tests/browser/test_client_browser.py` now clicks it for real and
hit-tests the centre; with the overlay restored it fails with "intercepts pointer
events".

**`appearance:none` and an explicit `height`.** WebKit ignores `min-height` on a menulist
and drew the select **19 px**, under half the floor, while Chromium honoured it at 36 --
measured in both on 2026-09-20. `height` is honoured by both. Stripping the native control
strips its arrow, so the chevron `#areaSelect` draws is reused beside it, `aria-hidden` and
`pointer-events:none`. This is the 2026-09-18 lesson again: one engine is not a check.

**An emptied list clears only the time.** It runs through `emptyMsg()` and `emptyActions()`
like every other empty state, which is what keeps `tests/test_list_status.py`'s pairing
rule holding -- a second empty path with its own `setListStatus` broke it. `clearTimeLink`
resets the time alone; `clearFiltersLink` still offers the rest separately.

**Verified in Chromium and WebKit at 320 and 1200 px in fi, sv and en**, 12 combinations
over a fixture straddling 18:00 exactly: 17:59 out and 18:00 in every time, the marks
`15:00 ... 21:30` half an hour apart under "Kaikki ajat", combining with the search, the
emptied state and its clear leaving a live search untouched, Leffat unaffected at 5 cards,
Ajat restoring the value, focus returning to the field, no overflow and no document scroll.
Retention across a date change checked separately on a day that has screenings.
Break-verified with thirteen mutations.

### Ajat's floor is now, and the reader can lower it (2026-09-20, sw.js v204)
**This reverses a recorded decision, on the maintainer's instruction and with a
measurement.** On 2026-09-01 a past-showtimes option for Ajat was dropped in the
seven-backlog-items pass: *"'Ajat' is browsing by time. Past showtimes are already
handled: ... `renderTimes` keeps past rows at 45% opacity with `pointer-events:none`."*

That reasoning answered the wrong cost. Dimming makes a row inert; it does not take it
out of the scroll. Measured 2026-09-20 at 18:34 Helsinki over the committed data: **257 of
449 of the day's screenings, 57%, had already started**, and 44 to 71% per venue in the
busiest files. In a combined city that is more than half the list read past before
reaching anything bookable. The other half of the reasoning has also changed since: v202
gave the view an explicit time floor, so there is now a natural place for this.

**One model, not two controls.** Ajat has a floor. With no mark chosen the floor is `now`,
so the list opens on what a reader can still get to. The reveal lowers it to the start of
the day. A chosen mark *is* the floor and overrides both, which is what keeps v202's
half-hour look-back meaning something: "alkaen 17:30" at 18:07 shows the screening that
began at 17:45, because that is what the reader asked for. The reveal stands down while a
mark is chosen -- offering two floors at once would be a puzzle.

**No new string and no new control.** `pastLabel(open, n, T)` already renders "Näytä
aiempi" / "Näytä {n} aiempaa" / "Piilota aiemmat" in all three languages for the cards and
the sheet, and `.pastlink` already carries its own 44 px of reach as a text-only link. The
reveal is both, beside the select. `state.showPast` is memory only, like `state.minTime`.
Past rows keep their 45% opacity and `pointer-events:none` once revealed.

**Verified in Chromium and WebKit at 320 and 1200 px**, over a fixture of six screenings
straddling the pinned clock: default shows the three ahead with "Näytä 3 aiempaa" and
`aria-expanded=false`; revealing shows all six as "Piilota aiemmat" with `aria-expanded=true`;
hiding returns to three; choosing 11:30 shows four, including the 11:45 that had started,
with no reveal offered; clearing returns to three. Break-verified with six mutations.

### The Anniskelu glyph sat above centre on a two-line ticket (2026-09-20, sw.js v205)
Reported from the live site with a screenshot. A regression from v198: the per-screening
language line made `.aud` wrap to two rows, and `.glyphs` is a flex item, so
`align-self:center` centred it **inside its own wrapped row** rather than in the
compartment. Measured before the fix: the glyph's middle sat **8 px above the ticket's**
in Chromium and WebKit alike, at 390 and 1200, on the card's grid stub and the sheet's;
exactly 0 on a one-line ticket, which is why it had gone unnoticed.

Taken out of the flow instead: `position:absolute; top:50%; translateY(-50%)` against a
`position:relative` compartment, measured 0 in both engines at 320, 390 and 1200. The
ticket also lost 3 px, 45 to 42, since the glyph no longer sets the first row's height.

**The reservation had to be stated twice.** `padding-right:24px` on `.stub .aud.twoline`
was simply ignored on the card, because `.stubs.grid .stub .aud` sets its own padding at a
higher specificity and won; the computed value stayed 8 px. With a long room name
("Tennispalatsi Sali 12") the ellipsised `.loc` would then have run under the glyph. The
rule now names both selectors, and the text box ends 5 px clear of the glyph in both
variants.

Not a contract change: `ticket.min_height` is a floor and 42 clears it, and nothing
`DESIGN.md` pins moved.

### A festival prefix is not the film's name, on the fallback tile (2026-09-20, sw.js v206)
Reported from the live site: the Rakkautta & Anarkiaa films at Cinema Orion had no
posters. 29 of the 30 R&A rows carry no TMDB match, and the tile made that worse than it
had to be. The two letters come from `title.match(/\p{L}+|\d+/gu)`, which splits on
letters, so `&` and `:` break "R&A:" into two words and **all 30 titles drew the identical
tile "RA"**. Measured with the client's own expression, not a whitespace split.

`tileInitials(title)` takes a recognised festival prefix off the two letters and off
nothing else. The prefix must leave something behind, or "R&A:" alone would tile "?"
instead of RA. "Ran" and "Rafiki: Ystävä" are untouched: the pattern requires the colon.

**This is display only and does not reverse the refusal.** `strands.py` refuses an "r&a"
entry in `EVENT_PREFIXES` because searching the *stripped* title would resolve one- and
two-word names -- Mouse, NOX, Redoubt, Blue Film -- onto the wrong film by popularity,
none of the 32 rows carrying a year. Nothing here reaches a search, a match, a cache key,
`normTitle()` or the displayed title; a test asserts those names are unreachable from the
block. Two rows were separately aliased after reading the TMDB record, which is what
`"r a mouse"` already did in the same 2026-09-19 pass that wrote the refusal.

`tests/test_release_year.py` pinned the old expression literally. It was rewritten to pin
what it guards -- the argument is `title`, never `cardTitle`, so "Carrie (1976)" cannot
tile as "C1" -- and break-verified by passing `cardTitle`.

### Landing-page descriptions are written for a reader, per booking mode (2026-09-22)
The `meta description` and the `og:description` beside it were one keyword line per page:
`{venue} ({city}): elokuvat, näytösajat, ikärajat ja liput lähipäiville.` for a venue,
`Kaikki elokuvateatterit ja näytösajat – {city}: {venues}.` for a city. Two faults. The
venue line promised `liput` for all 134 venues, including the 20 `door` ones that publish
no ticket URL at all and Heureka's planetarium, whose screenings are included in
admission: the fault the intro copy was already fixed for, and the description never was.
The city line spent its whole snippet on cinema names, 16 of them in Helsinki, and went
stale in the index whenever a venue was added or renamed.

`venue_desc()` now builds one opening sentence plus the ending the registry's `book` mode
settles, and `city_desc()` asks what is on in the city and names no cinema. Both published
languages carry six endings: `buy`, `reserve`, `list`, `door`, `admission`, and a neutral
one. Unlike `venue_intro()`, an unknown or missing mode does **not** fall back to `buy`.
A description is what a search result quotes, so a mode nobody has written copy for gets
the ending that promises nothing beyond the page itself.

Measured over the committed 134 venues and 17 multi-venue cities, in characters:
fi venue 153-198 (median 169), en venue 140-175 (median 150), fi city 149-155 (median
151), en city 135-141 (median 137). The test holds 110-220, which leaves room for a longer
cinema name without licensing a paragraph.

No Swedish. `build_pages.py` publishes `fi` and `en` only: `L` has no `sv` key, the head
carries no Swedish hreflang, and `lang_switch` sends SV to the app on purpose, which is
the deferred entry in `IDEAS.md`. Swedish description copy was drafted with this change
and deliberately not committed, because nothing in the generator would read it and dead
copy rots. Publishing Swedish landing pages is separate work, not a metadata change:
`L["sv"]` in full rather than the description alone, a `/sv/teatteri/` and `/sv/kaupunki/`
route pair, the language loop, the sitemap entries, a third hreflang on every page, the
page families the tests count, and README's page and sitemap figures.

Break-verified with seven mutations of `build_pages.py`, each turning at least one of the
new tests red: always the `buy` ending, an unknown mode falling back to `buy`, the opening
with no ending, `city_desc` returning the page title, `og:description` rendered from the
title, the description rendered unescaped, and the venue call site passing no `book`.

### The description's claim goes first, and the Finnish reads as Finnish (2026-09-22)
Review pass over the descriptions the entry above shipped the same day. Three copy
changes, no behaviour change.

**The claim was landing past the snippet cut.** `desc_door` and `desc_admission` opened
with "Samalta sivulta löydät myös…" and put the booking claim second. Measured over the
committed pages: on all 21 Finnish door and admission pages the claim began past char 120,
and on six of them at or past 155, which cuts to "…Liput myydään te". Both endings now
lead with the claim in both languages, at the same length: the Finnish claim offset is
52-60-83 (min, median, max) against 136-144-167, the English 57-65-88 against 105-121-144,
and no page hides the claim at 120 or at 155. `desc_buy`, `desc_reserve`, `desc_list` and
`desc_other` already led with theirs or carry none, and were left alone.

**The Finnish opening introduced a separator and a construction nothing else here uses.**
"Katso teatterin {venue} tulevat elokuvat ja näytösajat paikkakunnalla {city}." is an
appositive genitive in front of an uninflected name, which reads as machine Finnish on a
long one, and `paikkakunnalla` has no precedent in this file: `city_title`, `city_h1`,
`venues_h` and `city_link` all separate with an en dash. The opening is now
"{venue} – {city}: tulevat elokuvat ja näytösajat." and the city description
"{city}: Mitä elokuvia lähipäivinä esitetään? …". Neither inflects a city or a venue name.
The English copy is unchanged.

Lengths, re-measured over the committed 134 venues and 17 multi-venue cities (min, median,
max): fi venue 125-141-170, was 153-169-198; fi city 135-137-141, was 149-151-155; en venue
140-150-175 and en city 135-137-141, both unchanged. The bound stays 110-220. The Finnish
opening alone runs 49 to 82 characters, so an ending dropped from any page falls through
the floor, and the longest city name in the data reaches 143, so a city gaining a second
venue cannot breach the ceiling.

Only the reorder is pinned by a test, on a keyword rather than the sentence, so a wording
edit survives and a reorder does not. The Finnish rewrite gets no test: pinning
`paikkakunnalla` out of the copy would fail on the next legitimate edit, and this record is
the guard instead.

**Two limitations acknowledged and left as they are.** `desc_other` is unreachable from
committed data: all 83 providers carry a `book` in `DESC_MODES` (buy 49, reserve 16, door
15, list 2, admission 1). It is deliberate defence for the next provider added with a mode
nobody has written copy for, and only `DescriptionCopyTest` covers it. And `book` is a
provider field, not a venue one: `data/venues-*.json` carries `city`, `id`, `name` and
`short` alone, so a chain with one door-sales venue publishes the chain's mode for it.
That is pre-existing, shared with `venue_intro()`, and not introduced by `352b536a5`.

Break-verified with six mutations, each turning
`test_a_door_or_admission_ending_leads_with_its_claim` or its neighbours red: the Finnish
door and admission endings and the English door ending back to filler-first, the opening
with no ending, `city_desc` returning the page title, and the description rendered
unescaped.

### The analytics bundle is pinned by its bytes (2026-09-22, sw.js v215)
`PH_VERSION = '1.434.2'` pinned the URL the bundle is fetched from. It did not pin the
bundle. `sc.crossOrigin = 'anonymous'` was set and `sc.integrity` was not, so whoever can
change what `eu-assets.i.posthog.com/static/1.434.2/array.js` returns had script execution
on leffavuoro.fi. `analyticsScrub` is no defence against that: `before_send` is a callback
the library invokes, and the library is the thing being replaced.

**The hash.** `sha384-BmbtQMM1P8wo232drqi6RUQiNd0ZFk56bltD3yk2/94kez4jFURztoW+DlYzT2Ah`,
over the 313282-byte body that URL returned on 2026-09-22 at 00:39 UTC. Fetched once, on
the maintainer's instruction, and not re-fetched: two different hashes in one day is the
event this whole change exists to catch, and the answer to that is to stop and report.

**The cost, accepted.** If PostHog rebuilds that path the hash stops matching, the script
is blocked, `onload` never fires, `phOn` stays false, and `phQueue` fills to its 20-item
cap and drops the rest. Analytics stops and nothing on the page says so. It fails closed:
nothing gets mismeasured, there is just no measurement. The fix is to re-measure the hash in the same commit as any `PH_VERSION` bump, which is the next action
recorded in `IDEAS.md`.

**What the suite can and cannot show.** `phAllowedOrigin` requires `https:` and the exact
hostname `leffavuoro.fi`, so analytics never initialises under the browser suite's fixture
server and no test can load the bundle or be broken by this change. What the suite does
prove is the half that matters for the page: 37 tests in Chromium 151.0.7922.34 and
WebKit 26.5 drive the app with no bundle loaded at all, so nothing on the page depends
on it.

The hash itself was checked in a browser instead, on a local rig serving two script tags
against the real CDN URL, one with this value and one with a single character changed:

- wrong hash -- blocked, `onload` never fired, `window.posthog` stayed `undefined`
- this hash -- `onload` fired, `window.posthog` was an object

Chromium reported its own computed digest in the console error for the wrong tag, and it
read `BmbtQMM1P8wo232drqi6RUQiNd0ZFk56bltD3yk2/94kez4jFURztoW+DlYzT2Ah`, which is the
value being shipped, measured by the browser rather than by the openssl run above.

The success case on production is provable only after deploy, so it is checked once on
the live origin after the push and the result goes in the session report.

### One film, one card on a city page (2026-09-22)
A city page grouped its screenings by the published title, so a spelling that differed by
one capital was a second film. Seven pairs on the committed pages: "Keltaiset Kirjeet"
against "Keltaiset kirjeet" and "Myrskyn ikkuna" against "Myrskyn Ikkuna" in Helsinki,
"Oasis: Don't Look Back In Anger" against "... in Anger", "Spider-Man: Brand New Day"
against "... 2D" in Kouvola, and "Kojootti vs. ACME" against "(Dub)" and "(Orig)" in Oulu.
Found by a reader comparing cinemas in Helsinki, recorded in `docs/research/flow-review.md`.

The app had already answered this. `mergeKey` and `mergeIds` in `index.html` fold a title
key and `tmdb:{tmdbId}` with a union-find, and a city page is the app's combined view
rendered ahead of time, so the generator now uses the same two signals rather than a new
rule: `merge_key`, `merge_roots` and `group_by_day(merge=True)`. Theatre pages are
unchanged. One provider's own "(Dub)" and "(Orig)" rows are two entries in its programme
and two cards in the app's single-venue view, and merging them on a page the app does not
merge would be the same disagreement in the other direction.

The heading needed a rule the app does not have, because the app takes the first
screening's title and that is load order. It is the spelling most screenings use, then the
shortest, then codepoint order, all three deterministic because CI compares the pages byte
for byte. Where the TMDB id merged titles the title key did not, the count is not enough:
Kouvola held "Kojootti vs. ACME (suomeksi)" and "... (englanniksi)" as one card, and either
spelling advertises one audio version of a card holding both. `shared_head` takes the
opening the titles share when every remainder is a qualifier, which is the cinemas' own
text with nothing translated or added. It is asked only where the title keys disagree, so
"Keltaiset Kirjeet" and "Keltaiset kirjeet" can never become "Keltaiset".

What merging would have lost is carried on the ticket. Language already split per
screening when they disagreed; format now does the same, through the app's own `tagsOf`
and `stubTags`. Only what differs: a format every screening of the card shares separates
nothing and is not drawn at all, so a card looks exactly as it did unless the fold put
differing screenings on it. 2D never reaches a stub, and neither does a tag the room name
already says ("LUXE" beside "LUXE 3"). City pages only: a theatre page merges nothing, so
its rows keep their providers' titles and lose nothing. No CSS and no new element: the
format is a label part inside the stub's existing details span, beside the cinema, the
room and the language.

Measured after the change over the committed data: 0 within-day collisions, from 7; seven
groups are joined by TMDB id across differing title keys and all seven are the same film;
one group merges titles with no surviving distinction, "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and
"... 2D" in Kouvola, which is the marker `mergeKey` strips on purpose. 22 of 306 pages
rewritten, all of them city pages.

Break-verified with twelve mutations, each turning at least one test in
`tests/test_city_merge.py` red: the tmdbId union removed, a strip dropped from
`_MERGE_STRIP`, `shared_head` disabled, its floor lowered to 1, the spelling count
inverted, each of `stub_tags`' two filters removed, the card fold emptied, the format
parts extended to theatre pages, `shared_head` asked for every group, the merged group
keeping its raw title, and a duplicate `<h3>` written back into a committed city page.

### The wordmark carries the page's language (2026-09-22)
`/en/city/helsinki/` drew its wordmark as a bare `href="/"`, so Home from an English page
opened a Finnish app unless the reader already had English stored. Reproduced live and
recorded in `docs/research/flow-review.md`; the CTA beside it had carried `area` and `lang` since it was
written, and the wordmark never did.

It is now `/?lang={lang}` on every page, Finnish included. `startupLang()` reads an
explicit parameter before a stored choice and `remember` is false when a valid choice is
already stored, so the page a reader is looking at decides the app they land in and their
saved language is not overwritten by following a link. The Finnish pages carry it too
because the alternative is a rule with an exception: a reader with Swedish stored, looking
at a Finnish page, got a Swedish app from the wordmark and a Finnish one from the CTA.

`/status/` had the same shape and is a separate entry; `/tietosuoja/` has no language at
all and is a third.

Break-verified with two mutations of `build_pages.py`, each turning
`test_the_wordmark_carries_this_pages_language` in `tests/test_landing_pages.py` red: the
bare `/` back, and `lang=fi` on every page.

### The way back from a report is the screening, not the chooser (2026-09-22, sw.js v217)
"Rapportera felaktiga uppgifter" on a Kino Engel screening opened
`/status/?report=...&lang=sv#contact`, and the draft it composed was right: film, cinema,
date, time and a deep link to the screening. The way back was not. `← To showtimes` read
`/?lang=en`, the bare chooser, so reporting a screening cost the reader the cinema, the
open film and the day. `statusHref()` had been sending `area` from the footer link since it
was written; `reportScreening()` never did.

The app now sends both: `area` for the cinema, and `back` for this exact screening, which
is the same `screeningUrl()` the draft quotes, built once so the two cannot name different
screenings. The page prefers `back`, falls back to `area`, and labels the link "Back to
this screening" when it has one.

Language is written into whichever it uses, Finnish included. Two faults in one: a bare `/`
let a stored choice decide instead of the page the reader came from, and a return URL still
carrying the language the link was made in would have undone the toggle on this page. The
reader who switches to English here goes back to an English app on the same screening.

`back` is a URL off a query string and this page turns it into an href, so it is followed
only when it resolves to this origin, and it is rebuilt from `pathname + search + hash`
rather than passed through. Another host, `//elsewhere`, `javascript:` and `data:` all
resolve elsewhere and fall back to the area link; the harness covers each. The wordmark is
Home and keeps going to the area, never to the one screening.

The footer nav's accessible name was the hard-coded Finnish "Lisätietoja" in all three
languages and is now translated with the rest.

Break-verified with nine mutations: the origin check dropped, `back` ignored, the arriving
language kept, Finnish left without a parameter, an unknown language passed through, Home
pointed at the screening, the app sending no `area`, the app sending no `back`, and the
worker version standing still. Each turns at least one test in `tests/test_return_href.py`
red.

### The privacy page opens in the reader's language (2026-09-22, sw.js v218)
"Privacy" in an English app opened `/tietosuoja/` at the Finnish heading and the Finnish
introduction. The page holds all three languages, with `#fi`, `#sv` and `#en` sections and
anchor links between them, and the incoming link named none of them. Every link out of it
was a bare `/`, so a reader who arrived from an English app left in whatever they had
stored.

Two halves. The app's `privacyHref()` names the section and passes the same pair
`/status/` already gets, `area` and `lang`. The page rebuilds its four links out of that:
the wordmark, the back link, and the two footer links, with the back link and the footer
labels in the reader's language. Precedence is the app's -- the query, then `kino-prefs`,
then Finnish -- and the storage key is the app's, read and never written.

Not done, deliberately: `<html lang="fi">` is left alone, because the document holds three
languages at once and that attribute describes the first section a reader without
JavaScript lands on. Separate per-language privacy pages would also have worked and are a
larger change than the fault; the sections already exist and the fragment already reaches
them.

The page now carries an inline script, so `scripts/check_inline_js.py` covers it: five
scripts became six, and the test that counts them says why.

Break-verified with ten mutations: the section dropped from the link, the language dropped
from it, the footer link left static, the no-script href removed, the page ignoring the
query, the page ignoring a stored choice, the page rewriting the document language, the
back label pinned to Finnish, the footer links left alone, and the page dropped from the
inline-JS check. Each turns at least one test in `tests/test_privacy_language.py` red.

### A synopsis in another language says which (2026-09-22, sw.js v219)
The Swedish sheet for "Hetki ennen valoa" drew Swedish controls and Swedish screening
labels around a Finnish synopsis, with nothing marking the change of language. `synFor`
had preferred Swedish since 2026-09-16 and falls back to Finnish and then English, which
is right; what was missing was saying so.

`synFor` became `synPick`, which returns the slot as well as the text, and the old wrapper
was deleted rather than kept: one function and one fallback order, because a second copy of
that list is how the text and the label naming its language would come to disagree. The
sheet draws a caption above the description when the two differ, and puts `lang` on the
paragraph so a screen reader and hyphenation agree with the caption.

Not only Swedish. TMDB has a Finnish overview for some films and an English one for the
rest, so a Finnish reader is shown English text and an English reader Finnish text just as
often; the same caption covers all three.

Nothing is translated to fix this, and no title moves. The Finnish sentences are written
out per source language rather than built from a name, for the reason city names are never
inflected in generated text: "suomi" plus "ksi" is "suomiksi", and the three cases differ.

One CSS rule, on the muted token and a meta size the sheet already uses, so the caption
reads as a caption and not as a second paragraph of the description.

Break-verified with ten mutations, each turning at least one test in
`tests/test_synopsis_note.py` red: the note drawn always, drawn with no text, the paragraph
declaring no language, the note interpolated unescaped, the note moved below the text, the
Finnish name inflected from a stem, a source language left without a sentence, the note
given a placeholder that would carry film text, the caption style removed, and the open
sheet not redrawn when the toggle moves.

### An empty landing page names the cinema's next known date (2026-09-22)
Kino Engel's app view offered "Seuraava n\u00e4yt\u00f6s \u2192 Ma 28.9." and its landing page said
only that nothing was published for the next few days. Both true, one of them useful. 25
of the 134 Finnish theatre pages carried that sentence on 2026-09-22.

`next_show_day()` is the first date past the page's own window, read from the same
committed file the page is built from, so it costs a pass over shows already in memory and
no second fetcher. The sentence is appended to the one that was already there, in the same
element, and `day_label` supplies the date in the page's language and ends it with its own
full stop, so the line adds none.

Deliberately only where the page is empty: a page with showtimes on it is not asking the
question. Computing it anyway is equivalent by construction -- `page()` reads `next_day`
only in the empty branch -- and the guard stays because the pass is free to skip.

Break-verified with six mutations: no date offered, the window edge moved either way, a
past date counted as next, the latest date offered instead of the first, and the sentence
adding a second full stop. The seventh, computing the date for a page that has showtimes,
is equivalent by construction and is recorded here rather than covered by an assertion.

City names in `CITY_SV`, the language names, the privacy text and the rest of the status

### One Swedish vocabulary for screenings, schedules and the saved view (2026-09-23, sw.js v223)
The maintainer settled the terms the previous entry left open. Evidence read the same day:
[docs/research/swedish-vocabulary.md](../research/swedish-vocabulary.md).

- A screening is "visning": the empty states, "Kommande visningar", "Nästa visning", the
  age key, the footer actions, the status page's pending lines and the generated pages.
- The published schedule is "visningstider": page titles and headings, the intros, the
  stale line ("visningstiderna har inte uppdaterats"), the load failure, the status page's
  navigation and summaries, and the privacy page's two links.
- Data freshness is "uppgifter": the footer's source label ("Uppgifter: Finnkino") and the
  unread `behind` and `unverifiedOf`. "Visningstiderna är aktuella" stays because it
  states the result for the reader, not a provider's health.
- Subtitles are labelled "Textning:" in the app and on the pages, so the two agree.
- Descriptions read "Läs om filmerna och välj en visningstid för att ...", keeping each
  booking mode's own destination; admission says "kan du också läsa om filmerna".
- Door sales are "Biljetter säljs på plats": the sale can be at a box office or a café.
- The saved choice is "Din startvy" and the action "Spara som startvy", because a city or
  a region can be saved as well as a cinema; the saved state adds "öppnas vid nästa
  besök". The phone label stays "Spara".
- The status help heading is "Så tolkar du uppdateringsstatusen".

Kept as "föreställning": nothing in the Swedish chrome. TMDB and provider synopses are
published as sent and were not touched.

Checked at 320 and 393 px, light and dark, in Chromium and WebKit, against the served tree
with the service worker blocked and stale, partial and pending states injected by
intercepting the JSON: no horizontal overflow, no unnamed control and no clipped Swedish
string in 100 captures. The admission footer line wraps to three lines at 320 px and two at
393, unclipped; the stale banner to three and two. The saved-view heading was checked with
a cinema, a combined city and a region saved.

Settled the same day by the maintainer, sw.js v224: "Kommande visningar" for the list and
"Nästa visning" for one; Heureka's footer line says "Ingår i inträdesbiljetten", as its
generated page does; the subtitle label is "Textning:" only where it opens a label of its
own and "textning:" after the audio or another part of the line, in the app (`langTxt`'s
`lead`) and on the pages (`lang_parts`'s `lead`, key `subs_lead`). Heureka's page needed
no change: it already says the screenings are included and the ticket is sold on
heureka.fi.

Reported: at some window widths tickets grew to three lines, and at others they

lines at 900 px, where three columns squeezed to 245 px, and 11 at 1000; in WebKit a

### The stale banner waits for the worker's check (2026-09-23, sw.js v233 and v234)
After a day away the app opened with the stale banner although the committed data was
current, and it could stay until a reload. Two causes. The worker answers a schedule file
from its cache and refreshes it behind; the page drew that cached copy's age before the
refresh answered. And on a combined city the refresh could land before the city's slot
existed, since the members are prefetched at boot but the slot waits on the venue lists:
`onFresh` found no slot and dropped the message, and the older copy stayed. Reproduced in
Chromium and WebKit on `city:Helsinki` with a 24-hour copy in Cache Storage.

v233: `onFresh` remembers such venues and `loadSchedule` calls `filled()`, which re-reads
them from Cache Storage once. v234: the worker posts `{checked, ok}` for every data-file
answer, a failure included, beside `fresh`. While a file behind the selection is
unanswered and its data is late, `#stale` shows a neutral "Tarkistetaan päivityksiä…" in
#partial's colours; the warning comes once every answer is in, or at `FETCH_MS` (8 s)
from the oldest request. A failed or unreachable check is an answer, so offline shows the
warning at once. Data inside the window shows nothing while checking. A page under an
older worker gets no `checked` and falls back to the cap. `updateState` is the decision,
pure and sliced by `tests/stale_notice_harness.js`.

`tests/browser/test_update_check.py` runs the worker in Chromium and WebKit: early refresh,
slow, failed and unreachable checks, the cap, and a switch of cinema during a check.
Offline is modelled as a connection closed with no response, because WebKit's reload under
`set_offline` fails inside the engine. Seven mutations, each red in the unit suite or in
both engines.

(Chromium; 152 in WebKit) to about 20.

### A failed or unfinished load leaves nothing of the last venue (2026-09-24, sw.js v238)
Review finding #12 at c416446fd. `loadSchedule` drew the spinner and, on failure, the error,
but left `state` holding the previous venue's shows, stamp and sources. A filter tap, a
search, a view switch or a language switch calls `render()`, which drew venue A's films
and ticket links under venue B's name. The footer kept A's stamp, credited to B's
provider, because the credit reads the provider from the current area. The load now
empties that state before its await and again in its catch, and `render()` redraws the
spinner or the error while a load is unsettled. Covered in Chromium and WebKit by
`LoadLeavesNoOldVenue` in `tests/browser/test_client_browser.py`: a 500, a payload with no
`shows`, and a load held in flight. Six mutations, all red.

### A stored preference that is not an object reads as empty (2026-09-24, sw.js v239)
Review finding #20 at c416446fd. `prefs.get` returned whatever `kino-prefs` parsed to.
A stored `null` made boot's `prefs.get().lang` throw before the day chips were built, on
every load, in Chromium and WebKit alike (checked with a scratch Playwright run). `prefs.set`
could not repair it: `Object.assign(null, ...)` threw inside its own try. A number, a string
or an array was kept the same way. Anything that is not a plain object now reads as `{}`,
and the next `set` writes a valid object over it. The key is unchanged. Covered by
`tests/test_prefs_store.py`, which slices `prefs` out of the page through
`tests/prefs_harness.js`. Five mutations, all red.

### A language switch keeps the day the list was loaded for (2026-09-24, sw.js v240)
Review finding #13 at c416446fd. `applyLang` rebuilt the day chips with `buildDays`, which
takes the day from `savedDay()`, and then called `render()` on the list `loadSchedule` had
filtered for the old day. `savedDay` drops a day past the venue's horizon, and another tab
can rewrite it, so the chips could move while the list stayed. Reproduced in Chromium: 6.10.
at Orion, then Promenadi (horizon 17.9.), then Swedish, drew "I dag 14.9." over "Inga fler
visningar i dag." with an 18:00 on today. `buildDays(keep)` now selects the day on screen
when a switch passes it and that day has not passed; a day that moved anyway, past midnight
before any rollover, is loaded rather than redrawn. `LanguageSwitchKeepsTheDay` in
`tests/browser/test_client_browser.py`, three tests; four mutations, all red in Chromium and
WebKit.

### A combined view names a film by its group's sorted-first key (2026-09-24, sw.js v241)
Review finding #15 at c416446fd. `mergeIds` took the union-find root as a film's id, and
each join made the newer show's key the root, so the id moved with the order of the files.
Reproduced on the committed Kotka data with the page's own `cityPayload`: the Coyote vs.
Acme group was `kojootti vs acme englanniksi` with every day and `kojootti vs acme` with the
first day dropped, both member keys present each time, and a `#m=` link from the day before
matched nothing in `showSheet`. The group is now named by its sorted-first title key, each
show keeps its own key in `_mk`, and `showSheet` resolves a link through `sheetId`: the
group's id or any member's own key opens the film, so links made before this change still
open while their member is listed. `tests/test_merge_ids.py` through
`tests/merge_ids_harness.js`, three orders; seven mutations, all red.

### og:image is escaped like every other attribute on the pages (2026-09-25)

Audit finding G1. `build_pages.page()` put the first poster path into `og:image`
unescaped while every other interpolation went through `esc()`. The path is provider text
wherever an adapter publishes a relative `src`: `cinemahouse.py` unescapes the raw value,
and `mirror_posters` and `run.py` pass a non-http value through. A path such as
`data/posters/x"><script>alert(9)</script><meta x="` put a script element into the head of
the fi, sv and en venue and city pages. Now `esc(og_image)`. No committed page changes,
since every current path is a sha1 file name.

`HostilePosterPathTest` in `test_landing_pages.py` builds from the committed data with one
multi-venue city's posters replaced by that path, and reads the head of every page that
carries it in all three languages, city page included. It went red on the unfixed code;
removing the `esc()` again turns it red.

### The audit-fix client items, and the authorisation for them (2026-09-25)

The maintainer's written request of 2026-09-25 named five client items from that day's
audit (K1 to K5) for `index.html`, each with browser tests in Chromium and WebKit, and
K4 conditional on touching nothing `DESIGN.md` covers. Like the 2026-09-22 authorisation,
it covers those items and says nothing about the freeze being lifted.

### A tab resumed on the chooser past midnight rebuilds its day chips (2026-09-25, v244)

Audit finding K1. The `visibilitychange` handler returned on `!state.area` before its
rollover check, so a chooser left open overnight kept yesterday's chips and
`state.dateStr`; picking a cinema then drew "Tänään" over yesterday's date and loaded a
day that had passed. The rollover is now read first; on the chooser it rebuilds the chips
and fetches nothing, as before. `ChooserResumeRollsOver` in
`tests/browser/test_client_browser.py`, at 1200 and 375 px, Chromium and WebKit: it waits
for the venue lists (the picker opening) before the resume, because boot rebuilds the
chips once they land and a resume before that hides the bug. Red on the unfixed guard in
both engines, three runs out of three.

### Venue lists that failed at boot are fetched again on the next resume (2026-09-25, v245)

Audit finding K2. With `areas.json` failing at launch, `allVenues` stayed empty for the
life of the tab: the picker trigger and "Ja paljon muita…" returned at once and nothing
fetched the lists again, and an installed PWA has no reload control. The resume handler now
calls `retryVenueLists()` whenever the lists are missing, once the boot has settled so it
never races the boot's own load. On success the tab carries on as the boot would have:
the favourite or link the lists now confirm is opened, or the chooser is drawn without the
failure note; a retry that fails again waits for the next resume. `VenueListsAfterAFailedBoot`,
1200 and 375 px, Chromium and WebKit: `areas.json` answers 500, the trigger does nothing,
the list recovers, a resume, and the picker opens on Orion. The only wait not on the DOM is
a bounded poll of the fixture server's request log for the failed request, since nothing on
the page says the boot has given up. Red on the unfixed handler in both engines; removing
`bootSettled = true` turns it red too.

### A sheet opened during a resume refresh keeps the schedule on screen (2026-09-25, v246)

Audit finding K3. `refreshAll` emptied `jsonCache`, then waited on the venue lists (84
requests in production) before loading the schedule, so a film tapped in that window drew
"Ei näytöksiä valitussa teatterissa." with no ticket, and the sheet was not redrawn when
the load landed. The entries now stay until `loadSchedule({refetch: true})` assigns the new
payload over the one on screen; the others are deleted after it, so each is still refetched
on its next visit, and an open sheet is redrawn through `refreshOpenSheet`. The list itself
still shows its loading state while the schedule is fetched, as `LoadLeavesNoOldVenue`
requires. The background-refresh handler compares entries by identity and is unaffected;
its comment is updated. `SheetDuringARefresh`, 1200 and 375 px, Chromium and WebKit, holds
`areas.json` in flight, opens a card and checks its tickets before and after the release.
Red on the unfixed code in both engines; wiping the cache up front again, or dropping the
refetch so the refresh serves the old copy, turns it red in both.

### Ajat draws the chain legend on a full list (2026-09-25, v247)

Audit finding K4. `renderTimes` built the interactive chain legend and drew it only on an
empty list, while a chain filter set in Leffat still hid rows there: a city view with Orion
isolated showed Orion's rows with no legend and no "Kaikki" to undo it, although CLAUDE.md
says both combined views print a chain legend. The full list now carries the same legend,
above the time bar as on the empty one. It is the existing element with its existing
sizes; no `DESIGN.md` value is touched and `test_design_contract.py` passes unchanged, as
does `test_ticket_separators.py` in both engines. `TimesViewChainLegend`, 1200 and 375 px,
Chromium and WebKit, serves Promenadi's fixture file as Itis Helsinki for a second chain,
isolates Orion in Leffat, switches to Ajat and undoes it from the legend. Red on the unfixed
code in both engines; removing the legend again turns it red.

### The Finnish empty-day line names the selected day (2026-09-25, v248)

Audit finding K5, on the maintainer's written instruction of 2026-09-25. The 2026-09-05
copy pass above set `noshows` to "Valitussa teatterissa ei ole näytöksiä tänään.", and
that entry stays as the record of that day. `emptyMsg` shows `noshows` only for a selected
day that is not today, so "tänään" named the wrong day every time it appeared. It now names

näytöksiä pe 18.9." otherwise, the date's own full stop closing the sentence. Today keeps

julkaistu.", and the Swedish and English lines, which already said "this day", are
unchanged. `test_finnish_copy.py` pins the new string. `EmptyDayNamesItsDay` in
`tests/browser/test_client_browser.py`, Chromium and WebKit at 1200 and 375 px: tomorrow,
a later day, the unpublished case, both other languages and back, and at 375 px the line
fits with no sideways scroll. The first build printed "18.9.." and the phone screenshot
caught it. Restoring the old string turns 3 tests red, and dropping the full-stop rule 2,
in both engines.

### `index.html` is no longer frozen (2026-09-25)

The maintainer wrote on 2026-09-25: "I allow unfreeze of index.html". The freeze of
2026-09-14, recorded above with every change the file took under it, is lifted from that
date. Two rules stay: the page's design does not change (the instruction of 2026-09-17,
restated in the same message as "Do not make changes to design of the webpage"), and
`DESIGN.md` moves only on explicit written instruction naming it. The client rules in

### The pages' score ring prints the app's number (2026-09-25)

`scoreRing` as static markup and printed `str(tmdb)`, so a score of 8.0 read "8.0" on the
pages and "8" in the app, and its label "8,0/10" against "8/10". Vote counts disagreed at a
tie: Python rounds 1250/1000 to even ("1.2k"), `toFixed` rounds it up ("1.3k"). The pages
now print the score as JavaScript's `String()` does and shorten votes as `toFixed` does, on

a tie today. The ring's size, arc and markup are unchanged. `test_score_ring_parity.py`
runs the client's own `shortVotes` in node over 20,005 counts; 4 mutations, all red.

### A refused cache write no longer fails a data answer (2026-09-25, v253)

Audit finding K11. The data branch of `sw.js` awaited `cache.put` inside the promise that
answers a first fetch, so a write the storage refused (quota full) turned a 200 into a
network error for the page, and behind a cached copy it turned the check into a failure.
The write is now caught: the page gets the network's answer, nothing is stored, and
`fresh`, which tells the page to re-read the cache, is sent only when the write landed, so
a refused write cannot start a re-read of the old copy. `sw_fetch_harness.js` gained a
`put` that rejects; two cases in `test_sw_cache.py`; 2 mutations, both red.
`test_update_check.py`, which runs the real worker, passes in Chromium and WebKit.
