### The pages' merge key breaks words as the app's does (2026-09-25)

Audit finding E9. `merge_key` in `build_pages.py` carries the client's four `mergeKey`
patterns verbatim, and `test_city_merge.py` compared the pattern strings, but the same
pattern is not the same function: JavaScript's `\b` is ASCII and Python's is Unicode, so
"äsuomeksi" keyed as "ä" in the app and "äsuomeksi" on the pages. The two `\b` patterns now
compile with `re.A`; the other two keep Unicode `\s`, which is what JavaScript's `\s` is,
and `norm()` absorbs the whitespace the ASCII pair leaves. The client is unchanged, since
a lookbehind would be a syntax error on older Safari. No committed title keyed differently
and the pages regenerate unchanged. The new test runs the client's own `normTitle` and
`mergeKey` in node over seventeen hard cases and every committed title; 3 mutations, red.

### The venue lists arrive in two combined files, one per half (2026-09-26, v255)

Audit finding K6. Every load asked for one `data/venues-{id}.json` per provider, 82
requests plus 82 worker revalidations for 25 KiB, while the plain chooser uses none of it
until the picker opens ([research](../research/cold-load.md)). The single cloud-written
file first proposed was changed by the maintainer on 2026-09-26 to one file per half,
because a cloud-written file would have held the local half's venues and `pending` back
until the next cloud run. `data/venuelists-local.json` and `data/venuelists-cloud.json`
carry every provider file of their half verbatim (`scripts/providers/venuelists.py`);
`run.py` and `run_cloud.py` each rewrite their own half's file after a run, aborted runs
included, so each file has one writer. The client reads both and fetches a provider's own
file only when neither carries it; a missing or malformed combined file costs its own
providers a request each. The per-provider files stay written, the app's health and
freshness read the same fields as before, and the status page is unchanged. Drift:
`scripts/build_venuelists.py` in the Checks regeneration step and
`tests/test_venuelists.py` against the committed provider files. `robots.txt` allows the
new family. Measured, Chromium cold/warm: chooser 89/87 -> 9/7, venue 90/88 -> 10/8,
Helsinki 115/103 -> 35/23; WebKit 90 -> 10, 91 -> 11, 109 -> 29. Tests:
`test_venuelists.py`, `test_venuelists_client.py` with `venuelists_harness.js`, two in
`test_cloud_pool.py`, `CombinedVenueLists` in the browser suite at 1200 and 375 px in
Chromium and WebKit; 12 mutations red, and a thirteenth equivalent, whose guard was
removed.

### The status page reads the two combined venue files (2026-09-26)

On the maintainer's instruction, as a separate change from the app's. `makeStatusStore`
read one `venues-{id}.json` per provider for its health table. Its load now reads
`providers.json`, the two combined files and `areas.json`; a provider neither combined file
carries, which is the whole half when one file is missing or malformed, is read from its
own file. The choice is the app's `venueFilesFrom`, copied into the store and held equal to
the app's by `test_status_store.py`. Finnkino still comes from `areas.json`. Live refresh is
unchanged in shape: a worker message for a combined file reads it from Cache Storage and
puts each of its providers through the same `notBehind` and `key` tests a single file gets,
never the network; the message filter admits the new family. Each provider's row reads the
same as from its own file. Requests, Chromium cold/warm 86/86 -> 6/6, WebKit 86/87 -> 6/7.
Tests: five scenarios in `status_store_harness.js` and the parity check,
`StatusPageCombinedVenueLists` in the browser suite at 1200 and 375 px in Chromium and
WebKit; three request counts in `test_status_store.py` now count the two combined-file
requests a load makes in a world without them. 6 mutations, all red.

tickets itself and already kept every language on one line; phones are untouched.
Measured over all 151 views on 3.10. (118 with screenings) and 19 film sheets, in
Chromium and WebKit at 700, 1200 and 1440: cards whose one language broke two ways, 240
(Chromium) and 242 (WebKit) to 0; tickets without a glyph unchanged except 155 and 158
that a two-line neighbour had stretched to 59 px, now 44; no sideways scroll. At 375 and
699 px all 4,053 tickets measured identical in Chromium. `TicketLines`; 3 mutations, red
in both engines.

### The generated pages name every day by weekday and date (2026-10-04)
The maintainer's decision, option (a). A page is built for one day and read until the next
build, which after midnight was 2 h 15 min on a normal night and over 8 h when the local run
failed; until then every page called yesterday "Tänään" and today "Huomenna", in all three
languages. `day_label` now prints the weekday and the date for every day ("Su 4.10.", "Sön
4.10.", "Sun 4.10."), the form days three and four already had, and the "today" and
"tomorrow" strings are gone. No script and no schedule change. The limit that stays: a
past screening is still listed until the next build, but never under today's name.
`test_landing_pages` checks every day heading against its date's weekday. 2 mutations red.

The maintainer's decision. The clamped `.syn` is its own formatting context, so it could not

character clip and no control that opens the rest; the full text is the app's, as before.
`test_pages_layout`; 2 mutations red in both engines.

The maintainer's decision, the rest of P4-2. The six event names (`language_changed` and

### PostHog on the generated city and theatre pages (2026-10-07)
On the maintainer's instruction, to estimate use of the whole service, including readers
who never open the app. This reverses "the generated pages and /status/ stay
uninstrumented" of 2026-09-20; `/status/` and `/tietosuoja/` stay unmeasured.

Each generated city and theatre page, in all three languages, loads `/pageview.js` with
`data-category="generated_city"` or `"generated_theatre"`, async, at the end of `<body>`.
The 12 legacy redirect pages carry nothing. The file holds the app's scrubber, origin guard,
DNT/GPC check, pinned 1.434.2 bundle, integrity hash and init options. Its table allows
`$pageview` with those two categories only, and the URL sent is
`https://leffavuoro.fi/pages/{category}`. It requests the bundle after the load event.
`test_analytics_privacy.py` compares the two files and fails when they drift. The app is
unchanged, so no CACHE bump.

Measured on the wire on 2026-10-07 with the real bundle (sha-384 verified) under the
production origin, PostHog intercepted, Chromium and WebKit, Helsinki's city page and Cinema
Orion's page in fi, sv and en, each loaded with `?q=Carrie&utm_source=planted` and an
example.com referrer. Each of the 12 loads sent one POST to `eu.i.posthog.com/e/`, gzip, as
`{api_key, batch, sent_at}`, with one `$pageview` carrying `category`, `$current_url`,
`token` and `distinct_id` only. No planted string, path, city or cinema name appeared in the
body or URL. `Origin` and `Referer` were `https://leffavuoro.fi/`, and no cookie was sent.

posthog-js 1.434.2 drops every event when `navigator.webdriver` is true, the user agent
contains a listed bot name such as "headlesschrome", or `userAgentData.brands` names one
(its `_is_bot()`). A headless test sees the bundle load and no event. The measurement masked
those properties; the committed browser test answers the bundle with a stand-in instead.

Cost on a generated page: the tag is 74 or 77 bytes and `pageview.js` is 5,220 bytes,
2,325 gzipped, cached 600 s by GitHub Pages. On production without DNT or GPC there are two
more requests: the bundle, 313,282 bytes, 98,476 gzipped, cached a year and shared with the
app, and the event. At 375 px wide with 4x CPU throttling in Chromium, median of nine loads:
first paint 84 ms without the tag and 88 ms with it, the same 88 ms with PostHog never
answering, so the bundle is not the cause. The load event moved from 25 to 84 ms because
the async `pageview.js` is fetched first, partly route latency in the harness. The bundle
then ran as one long task of about 73 ms, after first paint in every run. WebKit, no
throttling: first paint 41 to 43 ms in every case, load 36 to 47 ms.

### An old empty answer is not repeated as current (2026-10-10, sw.js v278)
The live audit that day found Navettakino saying "Ei ohjelmistoa juuri nyt" under a banner
that its schedule had not refreshed for 88 hours, while the cinema's own page listed three
screenings. Its generated pages said "Lähipäiville ei ole julkaistu näytöksiä". The venue
was `pending` from a run on 2026-10-06, and every run after it had failed, so the empty
answer was four days old.

The app decides this with the same `staleNotice` and `STALE_H` as the banner. When every
venue in view is pending and one of them is past the stale window, it says "Ohjelmistoa ei
voitu tarkistaa" (sv "Programmet kunde inte kontrolleras", en "The programme could not be
checked"). A recent empty answer keeps "Ei ohjelmistoa juuri nyt".

A generated page is built for a day, so it counts days. A provider file written before the
day ahead of the build day (`PAGE_STALE_DAYS`) makes an empty venue page, or an empty city
page with one such member, say "Lähipäivien näytöksiä ei voitu tarkistaa." `--date
recorded` still reproduces the committed pages. The rebuild that day changed 12 pages: the
venue pages of Navettakino and Kinotour's three venues, in three languages.

Checked in Chromium and WebKit at 320 and 1280 px against the committed data: Navettakino
in three languages and Kinotour Kyrö in English gave the new line, and Kino Metso Muurame,
confirmed empty by that evening's run, kept the old one. Eight mutations red.

The page keeps `<html lang="fi">`, as decided on 2026-09-22, because it holds all three
sections at once. The live audit of 2026-10-10 found that the Swedish and English sections
inherited that `fi`, so assistive technology would read them with Finnish rules. Each now
sits in a `<div lang="sv">` or `<div lang="en">`, and the two link labels "På svenska" and
"In English" carry their own `lang` too. The anchors and the root language are unchanged.
Checked in Chromium and WebKit at 320 and 1280 px: the nearest `lang` is right for each
section, and the English heading and the page height match the previous markup to the
pixel. Four mutations red.
